name: xcorr
signature:
r = xcorr(x, y)
r = xcorr(x)
r = xcorr(___, maxlag)
r = xcorr(___, scaleopt)
[r, lags] = xcorr(___)
summary: The cross-correlation of two vectors, or the autocorrelation of one, at each lag, with the lags.
doc: $r(m) = \sum_n x(n+m)\,\overline{y(n)}$, the shorter vector padded with zeros, for lags $-L, \ldots, L$; L is maxlag, or N - 1 for N the longer length. scaleopt is 'none' (the default), 'biased' (r/N), 'unbiased' (r/(N - |m|)) or 'normalized' ('coeff': an autocorrelation is 1 at lag 0); a scaled correlation needs vectors of the same length. r is oriented as x; lags is a row. The lag of the peak, lags(k) for [~, k] = max(r), is how far y is delayed relative to x, negated.
differs: Matrix input, the correlations of all pairs of columns, is refused.
Integer-class input and empty vectors are refused.
At most 1,000,000 lags, and vectors of more than a few thousand elements at many lags are refused (the work is lengths times lags).

name: unwrap
signature:
Q = unwrap(P)
Q = unwrap(P, tol)
Q = unwrap(P, [], dim)
summary: Phase angles made continuous: each jump of at least pi between neighbours is removed by adding a multiple of 2*pi.
doc: Along the first non-singleton dimension, or `dim`. A `tol` below pi acts as pi. NaN elements are skipped: the elements on either side of them are unwrapped against each other, as GNU Octave 11.1 does.
differs: Arrays of more than 2 dimensions are refused; complex angles are refused.
